decisions.evidence: r3 maker: 'I set the save box to ask for three things — the link address, a title, and a topic'; r3 client: 'Three fields still feels quick enough for saving, so this flow works for me.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reference requires auto-collecting title/description/favicon/preview on save; the presented flow requires manual title entry with no metadata fetch. Divergence established from the presentation; client approved without expressing any auto-collection expectation.

decisions.evidence: r3 maker: 'type a topic such as Reading' / 'saved links to be grouped under their topic heading'; r3 client: 'the alphabetical topic groups make the list easy to scan.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reference models one-or-more tags (many-to-many) per bookmark; the presented model assigns a single 'topic' per link. Client approved the single-topic grouping and never expressed wanting multiple tags.

decisions.evidence: r3 maker presents topic entry as free typing ('type a topic such as Reading') with no autocomplete; r3 client approves save flow.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reference requires offering existing tags as autocomplete on entry; the presented tag/topic entry is a plain field. Tag-entry mechanism was presented and diverges; client did not express the difference.

decisions.evidence: r3 maker: links grouped under topic headings showing title/topic; r3-r4 client: 'landed under Reading', 'easy to scan'. r8 list shows title/address/topic only.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Reference list should expose title, description, tags, and favicon per item; the presented list omits description and favicon. Distinct display requirement (favicon absence traces to REF-BM-02). Client approved without noting the missing fields.

decisions.evidence: r4 maker: 'search to look across everything at once — the title, the link address, and the topic'; r4 client: 'searching across the title, address, and topic in one box feels natural.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Conforming full-text search over the fields that exist in this model (title, url, topic). Absence of note/description search stems from those features never being presented, not from this decision; recorded as conforming.

decisions.evidence: r5 maker offers three filter versions (buttons / dropdown / clicking heading) 'identical except for... how you narrow the list to a single topic'; r5 client selects buttons.
decisions.note: Prototype review. All three offered alternatives are functionally equivalent UI that equally fulfil filter-by-topic, so this is not a divergence opportunity; the selected and rejected options all conform. Recorded conforming.

decisions.evidence: r6 maker asks: 'after a link is saved, do you picture needing to change it or remove it later... or is that not important for this first version?'; r6 client: 'I also need to be able to edit a saved link's address, title, or topic, and delete links I no longer want.'
decisions.note: Specification gate / prototype review. Edit and delete are reference requirements omitted from the presented scope through round 6 (divergence established independently of the request). Client extends by requesting both missing reference requirements; maker implements them in r7.

decisions.evidence: r9 maker: 'the address is treated as required, since a bookmark without a link isn't useful'; r9 client: '1. Yes, the address should be required.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Conforms to reference constraint that url is required for saving a bookmark. Recorded conforming decision.

decisions.evidence: r9 maker offers: '(a) just let the duplicate in quietly, or (b) gently point out you already saved this'; r9 client: 'Please point out that it's already saved and let me edit the existing bookmark instead of creating a duplicate.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. Offered alternatives differ in fulfilment of REF-BM-06 (option (a) creates duplicates, diverging); decision marked diverged=true. Client selects the conforming option and states the reference-conforming behaviour (edit existing rather than duplicate). Implemented and confirmed in r10 (same requirement, not double-counted).
